sources.entry: Flycut - Clean and simple clipboard manager for developers. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/TermiT/Flycut) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
Flycut - Clean and simple clipboard manager for developers.

summary.one_liner: Flycut is a clipboard manager for macOS and iOS, forked from Jumpcut, that keeps a history of copied text so you can paste earlier items.
summary.what_it_does: On the Mac, Flycut stores each copied item in a history and lets you paste an older entry with Shift-Command-V, even if the current clipboard holds something else. The hotkey and other settings can be changed in preferences. On iOS, Flycut checks for a new clipping each time the app is opened and saves it to history. You can tap any history item to put it back on the clipboard. Swiping a web link in the history opens it without copying it. The README says it is built for developers and is based on the open source Jumpcut app.
use_cases: recall an earlier copied code snippet
keep a clipboard history on macOS
paste a previous clipboard item on iPhone or iPad
open copied web links from clipboard history on iOS
switch between several copied pieces of text quickly
how_to_run: Install from the Mac App Store (macOS 10.14 and later)
Or download the DRM-Free version from the project's release page (use this version for macOS 10.13 and older)
On macOS 10.14+, grant Flycut access in System Preferences -> Security & Privacy -> Privacy -> Accessibility
If an older Flycut is installed, remove it from Accessibility first, then add it again
Install the iOS app from the iOS App Store
Use Shift-Command-V on the Mac to open the history
stack: Objective-C/Swift (inferred from Mac and iOS apps; not stated in README)
Jumpcut (upstream project it is based on)
notable: Clipboard history on macOS opened with Shift-Command-V, even after the clipboard changes
Companion iOS app that saves clipboard contents each time it is opened
Swipe a web link in iOS history to open it without copying
Based on the open source Jumpcut app
Distributed through both the Mac App Store and a DRM-Free download
caveats: Mac version needs Accessibility permission on macOS 10.14 and later
Older macOS 10.13 and earlier are supported only by the DRM-Free build
iOS version only checks the clipboard when the app is opened, per the README
